## Discovery & Translational Science

* **Extracellular GPX3 enhances adipocyte insulin sensitivity independent of peroxidase activity** [biorxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.10.02.755889)
  * Discovered that secreted Glutathione Peroxidase 3 (GPX3) restores insulin receptor (InsR) expression and enhances insulin-stimulated AKT phosphorylation in white adipose tissue.
  * The mechanism is independent of GPX3's canonical peroxidase function and was confirmed using recombinant GPX3 in diet-induced obese mice.

* **ARumenamide AR-788 suppresses transient outward current in Brugada syndrome cardioids** [medrxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.10.06.26364857)
  * Generated human iPSC-derived right-ventricular cardioids harboring an SCN5A frameshift variant (p.A665Gfs*16) to model Brugada syndrome (BrS).
  * The novel benzylaminothiazole-benzimidazole carboxamide AR-788 inhibited the transient outward potassium current (Ito) concentration-dependently (extrapolated IC₅₀ of 25.4 μg) and restored BrS Ito to wild-type levels at 10 μM without reducing the sodium current (INa).

* **Aldosterone-driven MR activation mediates potassium-induced kidney fibrosis** [biorxiv](https://doi.org/10.1101/2022.06.15.496280)
  * Investigated renal fibrosis in murine models of unilateral ureteral obstruction and inducible podocyte apoptosis across dietary potassium levels (0.01% to 2%).
  * Showed that high dietary potassium promotes renal fibrosis via aldosterone-driven mineralocorticoid receptor (MR) activation in tubular and mesenchymal cells, which was tested pharmacologically with finerenone and genetically.

* **[Big Pharma] Baseline multi-omics predict tofacitinib response in ulcerative colitis** [medrxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.10.07.26364964)
  * Profiled transcripts and proteins in tissues and serum from active UC patients starting Pfizer's tofacitinib (10 mg BID) to identify biomarkers of histo-endoscopic mucosal improvement (HEMI) at week 8.

* **Resting-state gamma band power as a patient-enrichment biomarker in autism** [medrxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.10.06.26364877)
  * Compared EEG resting gamma band power in idiopathic autism spectrum disorder (ASD) to fragile X syndrome (FXS) reference samples to identify cortical excitability subgroups.
  * Notes that normalization of gamma power by BK channel positive modulators, such as Codabakalner, represents a therapeutic target.

* **Divergent iron metabolism regulation in pancreatic and colorectal cancer cachexia models** [biorxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.10.02.756162)
  * Analyzed iron metabolism in UN-KC-6141 pancreatic tumor-bearing mice and ApcMin/+ colorectal cancer mice.
  * Pancreatic tumor mice showed reduced plasma iron availability (-9.6% transferrin saturation, p < 0.001) and hepatic hepcidin upregulation (+100.6%, p < 0.001) leading to ferroportin downregulation (-42.4%), while the colorectal model did not share these alterations, indicating model-specific iron sequestration.

* **Endothelial Piezo1 regulates mechanically induced skeletal muscle hypertrophy** [biorxiv](https://doi.org/10.1101/2025.09.02.673617)
  * Showed that conditional endothelial deletion of the mechanosensitive cation channel Piezo1 in adult mice blunted muscle hypertrophy following mechanical overload.
  * The impaired growth was not due to poor vascularization or myonuclear accretion, but rather a reduced abundance of the protein kinase AKT.

* **Hypothermia-induced loss of protein O-GlcNAcylation in Bcs1l-mutant mice** [biorxiv](https://doi.org/10.1101/2025.07.08.660373)
  * Observed a systemic loss of protein O-GlcNAc in a Bcs1l-mutant mouse model of mitochondrial complex III deficiency.
  * Determined that the loss of O-GlcNAc is temperature-dependent and does not correlate with tissue levels of the substrate UDP-GlcNAc, which remained largely unaffected.

* **Dynamic near-term risk prediction model for immune-related adverse events** [medrxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.10.06.26364907)
  * Developed a multiscale XGBoost model to repeatedly estimate the 30-day risk of a first Grade ≥2 immune-related adverse event (irAE) every 21 days during the first year of immune checkpoint inhibitor therapy.
  * Achieved a pooled AUROC of 0.716 in a temporal evaluation cohort of 526 patients.

* **Proteomic signatures of environmental exposures across diverse populations** [medrxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.10.06.26364311)
  * Profiled 5,416 proteins in 10,043 participants from the All of Us Research Program to evaluate associations with more than 100 exposures.
  * Found that proteomic exposure signatures are highly consistent across populations and socioeconomic strata (<1% heterogeneity), with BMI-associated leptin trajectories serving as a notable exception.

* **Ocular toxicities of a novel anti-nectin-4-MMAE antibody-drug conjugate** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42850258/)
  * Characterizes corneal alterations, including combined limbal dysmaturation, microcyst-like epithelial changes, and corneal nerve alterations, associated with a novel anti-nectin-4-MMAE antibody-drug conjugate.

* **AI-based electronic health record screening for primary aldosteronism** [medrxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.10.06.26364909)
  * Developed an ensemble machine learning model (XGBoost, random forest, and extremely randomized trees) to prescreen hypertensive patients for primary aldosteronism using longitudinal EHR data from community and tertiary clinics.

* **Autonomic reserve moderates sleep-related phantom limb pain** [medrxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.10.06.26364856)
  * Evaluated 121 amputee adults using heart rate variability (HRV) and sleep quality indices.
  * A sleep × reserve × drive interaction (b = -0.51, p = 0.026) revealed that poor sleep predicts severe phantom limb pain primarily under high autonomic drive combined with reduced autonomic reserve.

* **Validation of an image-based surgical site infection detection AI model** [medrxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.09.22.26363636)
  * Evaluated performance differences (AUROC) of an image-based surgical site infection detection AI model across patient age, gender, geography, race, and skin color using Fitzpatrick and Monk scales.
  * Trained on 13,702 images from 4,274 patients post-procedure from multiple subspecialties.

* **Evaluation of the unsupervised PD-RISK Index toolkit for Parkinson's screening** [medrxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.04.30.26352172)
  * Tested a home-based screening tool for Parkinson disease in 305 participants, comparing typical PD, other neurological conditions, and healthy controls.
  * A simplified 11-item questionnaire paired with an 8-scent smell test successfully differentiated PD patients from healthy controls (p < 0.001).

* **CADENCE open-source software for cardiac optical mapping analysis** [biorxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.09.30.755844)
  * Developed a MATLAB-based open-source software application for signal conditioning, denoising, conduction velocity, and alternans analysis.
  * Validated the pipeline across datasets from four species (rat, rabbit, pig, human) and three camera configurations against three blinded expert observers.

* **Preoperative ultrasound and FNA diagnostic errors in papillary thyroid microcarcinoma** [medrxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.10.06.26364827)
  * Analyzed 180 consecutive cases (≤1 cm) and found that fine-needle aspiration (FNA) sensitivity was 44.4% overall, dropping to 14.1% for tumors <5 mm.
  * Identified 5 mm as the optimal size cutoff (AUC of 0.80) for diagnostic accuracy, noting that ultrasound specificity (69.6%) was compromised by the presence of larger benign dominant nodules.

* **Machine learning risk-assessment model for venous thromboembolism** [medrxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.08.18.26360687)
  * Analyzed 577,904 admissions across five NHS hospitals to evaluate the performance of an EHR-derived machine learning model in automating VTE risk assessment.

* **Digital screening tool ENTER for identifying community psychosis risk** [medrxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.10.05.26364756)
  * Developed and internally validated the E-DetectioN Tool for Emerging mental disoRders, a multimodal digital screener assessing symptoms, processing speed, and environmental risks in 2,522 participants aged 12–35.

* **Machine learning model for automated family relationship extraction from EHRs** [medrxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.09.18.26363428)
  * Used Random Forest classifiers to identify five relationship types (including Mother-Child and Sibling-Sibling) using the Indiana Network for Patient Care (15 million individuals) and validated against birth certificates.

* **Data preprocessing guidelines for passive sensing risk prediction in adolescents** [medrxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.10.06.26364884)
  * Established quality control and preprocessing standards for smartphone and wearable data from the Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development Study to improve machine learning risk prediction for substance use disorder.

* **Causal gut microbiome-amino acid pathways in emotional lability** [medrxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.10.06.26364911)
  * Conducted a multi-step Mendelian randomization study identifying 16 gut microbiota species associated with emotional lability risk, validating RUG013 sp001486445 via multivariable MR.

* **Bidirectional genetic links between ADHD and Big Five personality traits** [medrxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.10.05.26363336)
  * Used Mendelian randomization to support a vulnerability model where high genetic liability to Neuroticism and Extraversion, and lower liability to Conscientiousness, increase ADHD risk.

* **REM sleep infraslow respiratory rhythms correlate with neuropsychiatric symptoms** [medrxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.10.06.26364874)
  * Analyzed male veteran polysomnography and found that higher-frequency infraslow oscillations (~0.01 Hz) in REM respiratory rate correlate with severity of anxiety, depression, pain, and PTSD.

* **Rational modification of olive-derived 4-ethylguaiacol as a BBB-permeable acetylcholinesterase inhibitor** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42851142/)
  * Used molecular docking, density functional theory (DFT), and molecular dynamics simulations to design a blood-brain barrier (BBB)-permeable acetylcholinesterase inhibitor.

* **Berberine-enzalutamide synergy identified in prostate cancer models** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42850682/)
  * Used mechanism-informed language modeling and oxygenated 3D screening to discover a synergistic therapeutic effect between berberine and enzalutamide.

* **Acid-sensing ion channels as phase-specific targets in ischemic stroke** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42850478/)
  * Reviews the role of acid-sensing ion channels in amplifying and constraining neuronal injury during ischemic stroke, emphasizing a phase-specific framework.

* **¹⁸F-Flotufolastat PET/MRI detection rates at biochemical recurrence of prostate cancer** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42850466/)
  * Assesses the detection rate of PSMA PET/MRI using ¹⁸F-Flotufolastat at the initial onset of biochemical recurrence following radical prostatectomy.

* **Insulin resistance and 24-hour blood pressure variability in older hypertensive adults** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42850365/)
  * Identifies an association between insulin resistance and 24-hour blood pressure variability, potentially mediated by blunted sympathetic reactivity.

* **Novel RNA polymerase I and CDK combination therapy for aggressive AML** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42850350/)
  * Demonstrates the preclinical potential of a novel combination therapy targeting RNA polymerase I and cyclin-dependent kinases in aggressive acute myeloid leukemia.

* **Leveraging multi-omics and electronic health records for Alzheimer's target discovery** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42850312/)
  * Discusses methods for target and drug discovery in Alzheimer's disease using integrated multi-omics and longitudinal electronic health data.

* **New and emerging molecular targets for ADHD** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42851080/)
  * Synthesizes research on novel and emerging therapeutics and molecular targets for the treatment of attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder.

* **Distinction of meal quality and gut microbiota interaction via breath volatilome** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42850732/)
  * Evaluates how breath volatilome analysis in humans can distinguish meal quality and capture interactions with the gut microbiota.

* **Bayesian probabilistic statements for communicating clinical trial results** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42850643/)
  * Evaluates clinical trial reporting frameworks utilizing Bayesian probabilistic statements to communicate outcomes.

* **ACCEPT 3.0 recalibrated for global COPD prediction** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42850639/)
  * Validates and recalibrates the Acute COPD Exacerbation Prediction Tool (ACCEPT 3.0) for global application.

## Early Trials — Phase I–II

* **Resting-state functional connectivity unchanged in Long COVID cognitive rehab trial** [medrxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.10.05.26364531)
  * A randomized controlled trial of 58 adults with Long COVID and mild-to-moderate cognitive impairment evaluated a 12-week virtual cognitive rehabilitation and training intervention.
  * No significant group-by-time interactions were observed for resting-state connectivity within or between central-executive, default-mode, or salience networks (all p > 0.22) in the 39 participants who completed neuroimaging.

* **CBTi alters cognitive and emotional brain networks in adults with insomnia** [medrxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.10.06.26364880)
  * A randomized controlled trial enrolled 56 patients with insomnia and 20 good sleepers to receive either a 3-month cognitive-behavioural therapy for insomnia (CBTi) program or wait-list control.
  * Utilized resting-state and task-based fMRI (working memory, emotional reactivity, and face-name associative memory) to characterize short- and long-term neural changes.

## Late & Pivotal Trials — Phase III

* **[Biotech] Argenx Sjögren’s disease Phase 3 trial halted for futility** [STAT](https://www.statnews.com/2026/10/08/argenx-autoimmune-disease-study-sjogrens/) / [BioPharma Dive](https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/argenx-sjogrens-vyvgart-celiac-forte-study-results/832463/)
  * Argenx announced that a Phase 3 study evaluating its blockbuster FcRn inhibitor Vyvgart (efgartigimod) in Sjögren's disease will end early for futility following an interim analysis by an independent monitoring board.
  * The failure removes a potential $1.4 billion peak-sales opportunity and surprised analysts who expected results in late 2027, triggering a 15% drop in the company's share price.
  * Concurrently, Argenx announced successful Phase 2 results for a new drug candidate targeting celiac disease (the Forte study), which failed to fully offset investor reaction to the Sjögren's setback.

* **[Big Pharma] Lilly’s retatrutide shows weight-lowering efficacy in type 2 diabetes** [The Lancet](https://www.thelancet.com/journals/lancet/article/PIIS0140-6736(26)01987-2/fulltext?rss=yes)
  * A commentary highlights the results of the TRIUMPH-2 Phase 3 trial of Eli Lilly's retatrutide, a triple GIP/GLP-1/glucagon receptor agonist, in individuals with obesity and type 2 diabetes.
  * The triple agonist aims to overcome the historically lower weight-loss efficacy of GLP-1 receptor agonists in patients with comorbid type 2 diabetes.

* **[Big Pharma] Lower-dose tirzepatide maintenance shows heterogeneous response** [The Lancet](https://www.thelancet.com/journals/lancet/article/PIIS0140-6736(26)01433-9/fulltext?rss=yes)
  * Correspondence discussing the SURMOUNT-MAINTAIN trial of Eli Lilly's tirzepatide notes that while a 5 mg maintenance dose provides significantly better protection against weight regain than placebo, individual patient responses to the lower dose remain highly heterogeneous.

* **LATA trial shows benefit of long-acting injectable ART in African adolescents** [The Lancet](https://www.thelancet.com/journals/lancet/article/PIIS0140-6736(26)01952-5/fulltext?rss=yes)
  * The LATA trial, conducted across four African nations, demonstrated that long-acting injectable antiretroviral therapy (ART) can mitigate the adherence challenges of daily oral regimens in adolescents living with HIV.

* **Serplulimab perioperative trial in gastric cancer draws methodological caution** [The Lancet](https://www.thelancet.com/journals/lancet/article/PIIS0140-6736(26)01671-5/fulltext?rss=yes)
  * Correspondence and authors' reply regarding the ASTRUM-006 trial of perioperative serplulimab in PD-L1-positive resectable gastric or gastro-oesophageal junction adenocarcinoma.
  * Commentators urge caution before adopting the regimen as practice-changing, despite improved event-free survival.

* **NordICC trial colonoscopy screening data debated after 13-year follow-up** [The Lancet](https://www.thelancet.com/journals/lancet/article/PIIS0140-6736(26)01430-3/fulltext?rss=yes)
  * Correspondence debates the findings of the NordICC trial, which showed that one-time screening colonoscopy reduced colorectal cancer incidence but not mortality over 13 years.
  * Authors note that incidence reduction remains a primary benefit of preventive screening compared to early-detection-only screening modalities.

* **Port delivery system with ranibizumab evaluated for diabetic macular edema** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42850257/)
  * Reports the efficacy and safety results of the Pagoda randomized clinical trial, which evaluated the port delivery platform with ranibizumab (PDS) in patients with diabetic macular edema.

* **Lung ultrasound-guided fluid management trial in percutaneous nephrolithotomy** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42851149/)
  * A randomized controlled trial compared lung ultrasound-guided protocolized fluid management against conventional central venous pressure-based monitoring for tracking extravascular lung water during percutaneous nephrolithotomy.

* **Systematic review of indocyanine green-guided lymphadenectomy in gastric cancer** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42850302/)
  * A systematic review and meta-analysis of time-to-event data evaluated the survival outcomes of patients undergoing indocyanine green-guided lymphadenectomy for gastric cancer.

* **Meta-analysis of intraoperative red blood cell salvage transfusion in spinal surgery** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42850454/)
  * A systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the safety and efficacy of intraoperative red blood cell salvage transfusion during spinal deformity surgeries.

## Regulatory & Approvals

* **[Big Pharma] FDA approves Genentech's atezolizumab for Stage III dMMR colon cancer** [FDA](http://www.fda.gov/drugs/resources-information-approved-drugs/fda-approves-atezolizumab-combination-chemotherapy-stage-iii-mismatch-repair-deficient-colon-cancer)
  * The FDA approved atezolizumab (Tecentriq) in combination with a fluoropyrimidine and oxaliplatin for the adjuvant treatment of adult and pediatric patients (aged ≥2 years) with Stage III mismatch repair deficient (dMMR) colon cancer.
  * The agency also approved the subcutaneous formulation, atezolizumab and hyaluronidase-tqjs (Tecentriq Hybreza), in combination with the same chemotherapy regimen for patients aged ≥12 years weighing ≥40 kg.
  * Approval was based on the ATOMIC/ML39057 trial (NCT02912559) of 712 patients showing a significant improvement in disease-free survival compared to chemotherapy alone.

* **Safety review of mifepristone to continue into 2027** [STAT](https://www.statnews.com/2026/10/08/fda-mifepristone-abortion-pill-safety-review-continue-into-2027/)
  * The FDA announced that its ongoing safety review of the abortion pill mifepristone will extend into next year, drawing criticism from anti-abortion groups.

* **FDA flags safety signal with schizophrenia trial deaths** [STAT](https://www.statnews.com/pharmalot/2026/10/09/pharmalittle-were-reading-about-a-setback-for-argenx-lilly-suits-over-copycat-versions-of-an-obesity-drug-and-more/)
  * The FDA flagged a potential safety signal after four patient deaths were recorded in a trial testing an unspecified schizophrenia drug.

* **FDA issues guidance on postapproval manufacturing changes for biosimilars** [FDA](http://www.fda.gov/regulatory-information/search-fda-guidance-documents/postapproval-manufacturing-changes-biosimilar-and-interchangeable-biosimilar-products-questions-and) / [FDA](http://www.fda.gov/regulatory-information/search-fda-guidance-documents/questions-and-answers-biosimilar-development-and-bpci-act)
  * Released a final Q&A guidance document detailing requirements for postapproval manufacturing changes made to licensed biosimilar and interchangeable biosimilar products.
  * Concurrently withdrew Question I.20 from its March 2026 biosimilar development guidance, consolidating post-approval change details into the new document.

* **FDA updates Study Data Technical Conformance Guide** [FDA](http://www.fda.gov/regulatory-information/search-fda-guidance-documents/study-data-technical-conformance-guide-technical-specifications-document)
  * Issued an updated Technical Specifications Document representing current thinking on the conformance of study data submitted to CDER and CBER.

## Business & Strategy

* **[Big Pharma] Viatris acquires Pacira BioSciences for $1.65B** [BioPharma Dive](https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/viatris-pacira-acquire-pain-drug-zilretto-exparel/832481/)
  * Viatris agreed to acquire Pacira BioSciences for $36.50 per share in cash, representing a 45% premium and total valuation of $1.65 billion.
  * The buyout adds Exparel (bupivacaine liposome injectable suspension) and Zilretto (triamcinolone acetonide extended-release injectable suspension) to Viatris's pain portfolio.
  * Viatris is also awaiting an FDA decision on a fast-acting version of meloxicam, scheduled for December 27.

* **[Biotech] TRex Bio prices $117M IPO to advance Treg programs** [BioPharma Dive](https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/trex-bio-ipo-pricing-autoimmune-tregs/832297/)
  * TRex Bio priced its initial public offering at $14 per share, raising $117 million to fund its regulatory T cell (Treg) therapeutics.
  * Lead asset TRB-061, a fusion protein targeting TNFR2 on Tregs to suppress skin and gut inflammation, is currently in a Phase 1 study with topline data expected in 2027.

* **[Big Pharma] Roche partners with Defand Therapeutics for drug discovery** [STAT](https://www.statnews.com/2026/10/08/biotech-news-roche-goes-beyond-licensing-in-deal-with-chinese-biotech/)
  * Roche has established a discovery-focused partnership with Chinese biotech startup Defand Therapeutics that goes beyond traditional compound licensing.

* **[Biotech] Caribou Biosciences explores strategic options amid funding challenges** [BioPharma Dive](https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/caribou-reverse-merger-prospects-cell-therapy-private-public/832494/)
  * CRISPR cell therapy biotech Caribou Biosciences is highlighted as a potential reverse-merger candidate.
  * CEO Rachel Haurwitz noted that the difficult financing environment has made it challenging to secure capital for its clinical programs.

* **[Big Pharma] Eli Lilly files lawsuits over copycat obesity drugs** [STAT](https://www.statnews.com/pharmalot/2026/10/09/pharmalittle-were-reading-about-a-setback-for-argenx-lilly-suits-over-copycat-versions-of-an-obesity-drug-and-more/)
  * Eli Lilly has filed legal actions against companies producing unauthorized copycat versions of its tirzepatide obesity treatment.

* **[Biotech] Ovid Therapeutics initiated Overweight at Cantor** [X / Twitter](https://x.com/BioStocks/status/2108505705393136076)
  * Cantor Fitzgerald initiated coverage on Ovid Therapeutics (OVID) with an Overweight rating.

## Public Health & Policy

* **U.S. Census changes threatened by proposed administrative actions** [STAT](https://www.statnews.com/2026/10/09/health-news-census-changes-threaten-public-data-collection/) / [STAT](https://www.statnews.com/2026/10/09/2030-census-public-health-data-equity-morbidity-mortality/)
  * Public health researchers warn that proposed Trump administration changes to the 2030 Census—including eliminating questions on race, ethnicity, and sexual orientation and excluding non-citizens—could harm public health data equity.

* **Trump administration investigates universities for J-1 visa fraud** [STAT](https://www.statnews.com/2026/10/08/trump-administration-investigates-universities-j1-visa-fraud/)
  * The administration is investigating nine universities for alleged fraud involving J-1 visas, which are heavily utilized by international postdoctoral researchers.

* **MAHA movement struggles for midterm election foothold** [STAT](https://www.statnews.com/2026/10/09/maha-movement-rfk-jr-campaign-trail-midterm-elections/) / [Science-Based Medicine](http://sciencebasedmedicine.org/the-ebm-gurus-andmaha/)
  * The "Make America Healthy Again" (MAHA) movement, led by Robert F. Kennedy Jr., has maintained a low profile and struggled for financial traction in key midterm races.
  * Separately, commentators critiqued the movement's prominent anti-vaccine and unscientific statements, including claims regarding aircraft "chemtrails" and MMR vaccine safety.

* **Democrat proposes ending No Surprises Act arbitration** [STAT](https://www.statnews.com/2026/10/08/house-democrat-proposes-change-to-no-surprises-act-arbitration-process/)
  * A House Democrat has introduced a proposal to scrap the costly independent dispute resolution/arbitration process mandated under the No Surprises Act, facing pushback from healthcare provider groups.

* **Using Reddit NLP to evaluate post-Roe abortion access barriers** [STAT](https://www.statnews.com/2026/10/09/betsy-pleasants-stat-wunderkind-abortion-access-reddit-nlp/)
  * STAT Wunderkind Betsy Pleasants developed a natural language processing framework using Reddit posts to capture patient-reported barriers to abortion access following the reversal of Roe v. Wade.

* **Implicit bias in clinical trial selection** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42850489/)
  * Investigates whether provider implicit bias plays a role in the selection of patients for cancer clinical trials.

* **Opioid prescribing trends following 2016 CDC guidelines** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42850338/)
  * Analyzed changes in opioid prescribing and high-risk co-prescribing patterns among older adults with and without cancer following the implementation of the 2016 CDC guidelines.

* **Ambient UV exposure linked to lower cardiovascular and cancer mortality** [medrxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.10.06.26364908)
  * An ecological analysis of US Health Service Areas, corroborated by UK Biobank data (412,665 individuals), identified an inverse association between long-term ambient ultraviolet exposure and cardiovascular and cancer mortality.

* **COVID-19 secondary bacterial and fungal infections in UK hospitals** [medrxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.10.07.26363238)
  * An ISARIC/WHO and UKHSA linkage study of 173,947 hospitalized COVID-19 episodes found that 5.8% of patients had preceding, co-, or secondary bacterial/fungal infections. Secondary infections were most common (3.5%), with Escherichia coli (29.6%) and Staphylococcus aureus (15.2%) being the most frequent isolates.

* **Socioeconomic deprivation impacts chronic subdural hematoma outcomes** [medrxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.10.07.26364832)
  * A single-center retrospective study in the UK found that Index of Multiple Deprivation categories significantly correlate with initial length of stay and subsequent days hospitalized in patients treated surgically for CSDH.

* **National prevalence of concurrent wasting and stunting in Yemeni children** [medrxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.10.06.26364923)
  * Analyzed the 2022–2023 Yemen Multiple Indicator Cluster Survey (17,734 children under 5) to establish the national burden and socioeconomic determinants of concurrent wasting and stunting.

* **Data duplicity in Brazilian digital healthcare systems** [medrxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.10.06.26364925)
  * Assessed the database structure of the SUSfacilMG digital care-regulation system in Brazil, identifying that 40% of the 1,586 tables contained repeated descriptive attributes such as patient identifiers.

* **Inflammation mediators of chemical-mixture-induced steatotic liver disease** [medrxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.10.06.26364867)
  * Evaluated NHANES data (1999–2020) from 39,061 U.S. adults, finding associations between latent environmental chemical mixtures (using PCP-PCA) and MASLD, mediated by inflammatory biomarkers.

* **Engagement of sub-Saharan African palliative care patients in research** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42850672/)
  * Developed best-practice guidelines for involving and engaging palliative care patients in clinical research in sub-Saharan Africa.

* **PISA 2025 results point to declining adolescent health literacy competencies** [The Lancet](https://www.thelancet.com/journals/lancet/article/PIIS0140-6736(26)01906-9/fulltext?rss=yes)
  * Analysis of the 2025 PISA results across 760,000 students in 91 countries warns of declining reading, math, and science competencies, which underpin modern health literacy in the age of AI.

* **Canadian prison formulary changes spark clinical protests** [The Lancet](https://www.thelancet.com/journals/lancet/article/PIIS0140-6736(26)02039-8/fulltext?rss=yes)
  * Mental health experts have criticized changes to the drug formulary for 14,000 Canadian prisoners, arguing they are inconsistent with clinical best practices.

* **Mass drug administration for scabies in the South Pacific** [The Lancet](https://www.thelancet.com/journals/lancet/article/PIIS0140-6736(26)02040-4/fulltext?rss=yes)
  * Highlights mass drug administration programs pioneered by Fiji and the Solomon Islands to control endemic scabies.

* **Regulating prospective development of medical AI** [The Lancet](https://www.thelancet.com/journals/lancet/article/PIIS0140-6736(26)01941-0/fulltext?rss=yes)
  * Correspondence urges regulators to establish clinical necessity and safety boundaries before medical AI tools are prospectively developed, rather than debating ethics after deployment.

* **Taiwan integrated screening-to-cure path for Hepatitis C elimination** [The Lancet](https://www.thelancet.com/journals/lancet/article/PIIS0140-6736(26)01812-X/fulltext?rss=yes)
  * Details Taiwan's progress toward the WHO 2030 hepatitis C elimination goal via a comprehensive, integrated screening-to-cure clinical cascade.

* **Code sharing remains limited in clinical prediction model research** [Nature Medicine](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41591-026-04691-1)
  * An AI-assisted scoping review of open-access published literature reveals limited code availability and significant variability in documentation quality for clinical prediction models.

***

**Worth watching:** The FDA's safety review timeline for mifepristone extending into 2027, and the upcoming December 27 action date for Viatris's fast-acting meloxicam.

- Biology & Health
    - [Healthcare Apps Won’t Take Over the World](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/ot2cKnSeDZ0) -- Digital Health Inside Out
        - Discusses why building connectors or APIs on existing electronic health record (EHR) platforms like Epic carries more practical market impact than standalone healthcare apps.
        - Explains that standalone digital health applications frequently overestimate their capability to independently transform the healthcare market.
        - Highlights the necessity of integrating directly into dominant clinical workflows rather than expecting providers to adopt isolated solutions.
    - [We Thought K Health Was Dead. CEO Allon Bloch Came on Our Podcast to Prove Us Wrong.](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xBnb5TXtNig) -- Digital Health Inside Out
        - Details K Health's strategic pivot from a direct-to-consumer symptom checker to an enterprise clinical AI platform integrated into major health systems, including Mayo Clinic and Mass General Brigham.
        - Covers the architecture of PatientGPT, an agentic AI system that coordinates patient intake, clinical conversations, electronic health record analysis, scheduling, and physician documentation.
        - Discusses clinical safety engineering, specifically how K Health trains its models to output "I don't know" to prevent hallucinations in high-stakes medical contexts.
        - Addresses competitive dynamics against general-purpose foundation models (OpenAI) and dominant EHR systems (Epic), focusing on real-world medical data and deep workflow integration as defensible moats.
        - Examines healthcare AI economics, commercialization timelines, and governance challenges when health systems serve simultaneously as enterprise customers and equity investors.
- Pure Science
    - [What is edge dislocation?](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/j9p3Sn8ROL4) -- Veritasium
        - Demonstrates the physics of crystal lattices and structural defects using a physical bubble raft model.
        - Visualizes edge dislocation, illustrating how extra half-planes of atoms shift within a crystalline structure.
        - Shows how macroscopic bubble arrays simulate microstructural phenomena at the atomic scale.
    - [L'IA va-t-elle tuer les maths ? — L'interview d'Hugo Duminil-Copin](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HJFk7D5Vufc) -- ScienceEtonnante

        - Explores recent AI-driven developments regarding specific open mathematical problems, including Erdős' unit distance conjecture, percolation theory ($\theta_{p_c}$), and the Navier-Stokes Millennium Prize problem.
        - Analyzes the mathematical community's reaction to automated reasoning tools and how AI assistance will redefine the role and training of future mathematicians.
